headline: UN Votes to Replace 450-Year-Old Map That Shrinks Africa
meta_description: 164 countries voted to replace the Mercator projection with Equal Earth, correcting a cartographic distortion that made Africa appear 14 times smaller than rea…
summary_short: On September 5, 2026, the UN General Assembly voted to replace the Mercator map with a more accurate projection, finally correcting a 457-year-old geographic misrepresen…
body:
For nearly half a millennium, the Mercator map has hung in classrooms and government offices worldwide, depicting Greenland and Africa as roughly equal in size—a mathematical impossibility. Greenland actually covers 2.2 million square kilometers while Africa spans 30.4 million, making the distortion a factor of 14. On September 5, 2026, that era ended when 164 countries voted to adopt the UN resolution "Correct the Map," replacing the 1569 projection with the more accurate Equal Earth projection. Only the United States opposed the measure, with six nations abstaining.

The Mercator map was designed by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to aid European navigators, but its mathematical compromise—expanding polar regions to show Earth's curved surface on a flat page—has warped global perception for centuries. Africa's misrepresentation runs deeper than cartography: advocates argue it has subtly diminished the continent's perceived resources, population, and investment potential in the minds of policymakers and students alike. As Lerato Mogoatlhe of Africa No Filter explained, the problem is "not just a cartographic error. It is a narrative issue."

The African Union's 54 member states formally adopted Equal Earth in February 2026, with Togo sponsoring the UN resolution and France pledging to stop using Mercator in its ministry. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot framed the shift philosophically: "Correcting a representation that distorts [the world] is already an act of truth." While the resolution is non-binding, institutions worldwide are expected to gradually transition to the corrected projection. The Equal Earth map shows what was always true: Africa could fit the entire United States, China, India, Japan, Mexico, and much of Europe inside its borders with room remaining.
quick_facts: 164 countries voted September 5, 2026 to replace the Mercator map
Mercator distorted Africa's size by a factor of 14 for 457 years
African Union's 54 member states formally adopted Equal Earth in February 2026
Only the United States voted against the UN resolution
